# VantaDB — ThreadSanitizer suppressions (job `sanitizer-tsan`, FIND-737)
#
# One entry per CLASS, never per report. The lane used to be retired because a
# run produced 243 reports that no one could adjudicate (CI_POLICY § TSan lane).
# Enumerating those 243 as lines is what this file exists to avoid: TSan prints
# `Suppressions used:` at exit, so a class that starts matching again arrives as
# ONE named line instead of a wall of warnings.
#
# HOW A LINE IS READ (measured, not assumed):
#   - matched as a substring, with `*` implied at both ends, against FUNCTION
#     names and FILE names of both stacks (reporting stack and, for races, the
#     previous-access stack); `^` / `$` anchor to the whole name.
#   - a line here is a CLAIM: "this class cannot be an engine finding".
#
# HARD INVARIANT — do not break it: never suppress a name containing `vantadb`
# nor a `src/` file. The lane's only product is "no report has an engine frame";
# an entry naming engine code makes that rule unmeasurable, which is the same
# blindness the lane was retired for (warn #42, kernels.rs:275, carried no
# harness and no dependency frame — a real double-free in FjallInner's teardown
# prints the same shape).
#
# The job warns (does not fail) when a class below starts firing: the failure
# criterion is the engine-frame rule alone. A firing class is rot to re-reason,
# the lesson `suppression hits: 0` taught in 24 h (FIND-714).
#
# With `-Zbuild-std` these classes are expected to fire ZERO times: an
# instrumented `std` sees its own futex and atomics. That is why they are
# active here — they are the shape of the regression to watch, not tape.

# class: libtest's own event plumbing — an Arc<Mutex<Option<..>>> owned by the
# harness. 176 of the 243 reports. The disputed accesses are inside libtest.
race:^test::run_test

# class: std::sync::Mutex, the futex path (58 + 8 of the 243 — fjall/flume
# teardown and tokio's blocking pool). A futex is not a pthread_mutex, so the
# libc interceptor never fires; only an instrumented std sees it.
race:^std::sys::sync::mutex

# class: std::sync::Once / OnceLock, the futex-based one-time init (report #42:
# select_kernels() -> KERNELS.get_or_init). `core::mem::MaybeUninit::write` and
# `OnceLock::initialize` are the frames that made it look engine-local.
race:^std::sys::sync::once

# class: `Arc` refcounts — the drop path in alloc. Shape-compatible with a real
# double free, which is exactly why the engine-frame rule below it stays armed.
race:^alloc::sync::Arc
